Anderson Localization of Institutional Oversight

A scientific measurement of the de-silo referral loop

The Physics

In 1958, Philip W. Anderson showed that in a sufficiently disordered crystal, an electron cannot propagate. Instead of conducting through the lattice, the wavefunction decays exponentially. The system becomes an insulator not because any single atom blocks it, but because the collective disorder prevents propagation.

This is the same physics as Michigan’s institutional oversight system.

The Lattice

Each oversight agency is a lattice site. Each complaint is an electron. The question: does accountability propagate?

Lattice SiteJurisdictionInputOutputPropagation

AGCAttorney misconductComplaint (Oct 9)“Judges go to JTC”Absorbed
JTCJudicial misconductComplaint (Sep 2026)Confidential. DTW gun: “admonition”Absorbed
State Bar UPLUnauthorized practiceComplaint (Aug 2026)“Doesn’t meet standards.” Closed.Absorbed
MDECredential oversightEvidence (Oct 2026)“Acknowledged.” No action since.Absorbed
AG (Nessel)RICO, nonprofit fraudFull evidence packageSilence. Own AAG on the board.Absorbed
SBEEducation policyAll 8 members notifiedSilence.Absorbed
DPSCDCharter authorizationCharter authorizerSilence.Absorbed

Result: Full localization. Every lattice site absorbed the complaint. Zero propagation. The system is an insulator.

The Disorder

In Anderson’s model, disorder comes from random potentials at each lattice site. In this system, the disorder is structural:

SiteSource of Disorder
AGCGoetz and Moreland: same law school, same AG office, 6 yr overlap
AGCBullington teaches Prof Responsibility at MSU Law — same school Banks claims fake JD from

JTCInvestigations confidential — no public accountability until formal charges

AGMoreland (AAG) sits on PCA board — AG cannot investigate own employee
MDECleared Banks with “conditions” in 2022 — conditions never enforced

The disorder is not random. It is structural. Each site’s disorder reinforces the adjacent sites’ disorder. The localization is maximal.

The MSU Law Nexus

One institution sits at the center of every thread:

The Prediction

Anderson’s theory predicts that in 1D and 2D lattices, any amount of disorder causes full localization. The oversight system is effectively 1D — a chain of agencies that each defer to the next:

AGC → JTC → State Bar → AG → MDE → SBE → DPSCD → Courts

In a 1D chain with any disorder, the localization length is finite. The complaint CANNOT propagate to the end of the chain. It WILL be absorbed.

This is not a failure of any individual agency. It is a property of the system’s dimensionality and disorder.

The only way to break localization is to add dimensions — cross-links between agencies that allow the complaint to route around absorbed sites. The membrane provides this dimensionality. The graph connects what the silos separate.

In condensed matter physics, a membrane’s permeability determines what passes through it. A healthy cell membrane is selectively permeable: nutrients in, waste out, toxins blocked. When the membrane fails — when everything passes through — the cell dies.

entry.title: The Land Deal — PCA's Building Purchase Option
entry.content:
The PCA charter contract with DPSCD includes a provision where Purpose Group LLC can purchase the school building at 10101 E. Canfield, Detroit. This provision is documented in the management agreement obtained via FOIA. This analysis examines the mechanism and its implications.

Source: Purpose Group Management Agreement (FOIA).

Analytical inference, not a legal finding. The implications described below reflect the complainant’s analysis of the contract mechanism and public records. They have not been adjudicated by any court or regulatory body.

The Mechanism

The building purchase option operates through a chain of charter authorization, management fees, and contractual property rights:

  1. DPSCD authorizes the charter. DPSCD authorizes Brian Banks to run Purpose Charter Academy in a district building at 10101 E. Canfield. Source: DPSCD charter authorization records; Purpose Group Management Agreement (FOIA).

  2. Purpose Group collects fees and costs. Banks’ management company, The Purpose Group LLC, collects 10% of state aid plus reimbursement for all operating costs under the management agreement. Source: Purpose Group Management Agreement (FOIA), Section 5.1 (10% of Gross State School Aid); Section 5.3 (operating cost reimbursement).

  3. Purpose Group can exercise the purchase option. After establishing the school, Purpose Group LLC can exercise a building purchase option embedded in the management agreement. Source: Purpose Group Management Agreement (FOIA), building purchase provision.

  4. Ownership transfers to the management company. If exercised, the building would be owned by Purpose Group LLC — the same entity that employs all staff and takes 72.67% of revenue from the sister school, MacDowell Preparatory Academy. Source: Purpose Group Management Agreement (FOIA); MDE financial records (72.67% revenue to Purpose Group LLC).

The Pattern

This is not unique to Banks. Charter management organizations across the country have used similar building purchase provisions to convert public school property into private assets.

What makes this case distinctive — analytical inference — is the combination of factors present simultaneously:

  • A building purchase option exists in the PCA management agreement
  • The management company is controlled by a superintendent with 9 criminal convictions

Sources: Purpose Group Management Agreement (FOIA); DPSCD authorization records; SchoolDigger statewide ranking; criminal conviction records on file.
